items.title: Meta Ads: $363.66 spend, 28 leads, $12.99 CPL — Flooring Problems Campaign
items.summary: This run widened to 2026-09-08 through 2026-09-14 (7 days, capped) to cover the gap since the last successful pull (which ended 2026-09-07) — Meta spent $363.66, all on the sole actively-delivering campaign, Flooring Problems Campaign, generating 28 leads at $12.99 CPL. That's in line with (slightly better than) the prior 7-day baseline (2026-09-01 to 2026-09-07: $335.95 / 24 leads, ~$14.00 CPL), so no anomaly; account is ACTIVE and no ads are flagged. Three other campaigns (Tiles Carasoul 1.99, Dead Stock Inventory Campaign Campaign, Real Estate List Building) remain PAUSED with no budget.

needs_attention: Last successful meta-ads.json in this branch's ingest/ history is 2026-09-08 (window ending 2026-09-07) — no meta-ads.json exists for 2026-09-09 through 2026-09-14 here. Widened this pull to --days 7 (2026-09-08 to 2026-09-14, the full gap, at the 7-day cap) to cover it. Note per this repo's recurring pattern: prior 'gaps' have repeatedly turned out to be branch-isolation artifacts (runs that happened but stayed on unmerged session branches, invisible to main-agents) rather than real misses — that was not independently re-verified across branches here, so if a meta-ads.json for part of 2026-09-09 through 2026-09-14 later surfaces on an unmerged branch, treat that overlap as already covered by this widened pull rather than double-counted.

Flooring Problems Campaign's raw actions again include lead-like conversion types outside the script's documented LEAD_ACTION_TYPES set (offsite_complete_registration_add_meta_leads, offsite_search_add_meta_leads, offsite_content_view_add_meta_leads — each valued at 28, exactly matching the counted leads), consistent with prior flags on 2026-08-31, 2026-09-02, and 2026-09-07/2026-09-08. No discrepancy in the counted total, but this is now a recurring pattern across many runs — the script's LEAD_ACTION_TYPES set should be extended rather than continuing to hand-note it.

This pull's 7-day window returned one aggregated row per campaign (Meta's campaign-level insights here don't break out by day), so day-level anomaly checks — e.g. whether the ACTIVE campaign delivered on every individual day within the gap — could not be evaluated per-day, only in aggregate across the whole window, which showed normal delivery throughout.
